# Kāmāvacarakusala (Ds 2.1.1)
**ID:** Ds 2.1.1
**Section:** Dhammasaṅgaṇī (ds)

## AI-generated Overview (from reference literature and SuttaCentral)
*This overview was drafted by an AI model from the cited scholarship and SuttaCentral data and may contain errors; verify against the sources before relying on it.*
The *Kāmāvacarakusala* ("Wholesome [Consciousness] of the Sense Sphere") is the opening analytical section of the *Cittuppādakaṇḍa* (the book on the arising of consciousness) in the *Dhammasaṅgaṇī*, the first treatise of the Abhidhamma Piṭaka [Hazra 1994; SuttaCentral]. Following the matrix (*mātikā*) of wholesome phenomena (*kusala-dhammā*), the text systematically analyzes sense-sphere wholesome states (*kāmāvacara-kusala-dhammā*) by distinguishing eight fundamental types of consciousness (*citta*) [Gethin 2001; Bodhi 1999]. These eight consciousnesses are categorized through three intersecting dichotomies: affective tone, divided between mental joy (*somanassa*) and equanimity (*upekkhā*); cognitive orientation, being either associated with knowledge (*ñāṇasampayutta*) or dissociated from it (*ñāṇavippayutta*); and volitional activation, whether unprompted (*asaṅkhārika*) or prompted (*sasaṅkhārika*) [Bodhi 1999]. For each consciousness type, the text presents an exhaustive inventory of its constituent mental factors (*cetasika*), such as contact (*phassa*) and volition (*cetanā*) [Devdas 2004]. In her study and translation of the *Dhammasaṅgaṇī*, C. A. F. Rhys Davids notes the distinctive canonical phraseology of the manual (such as *kāmāvacaraṁ kusalaṁ*) in contrast to later commentarial idiom [Rhys Davids 1900].
Curated parallels recorded on SuttaCentral connect the text to passages in the *Mahāniddesa* (Mnd 2, 8, 16) and the *Cullaniddesa* (Cnd 5, 17, 23), along with structural resemblances to Mnd 6 and the *Rūpavibhatti* (Ds 2.2.3) [SuttaCentral]. DharmaNexus detects massive Pali-internal text reuse (12,701 matching passages across 151 texts), reflecting shared structural formulas with neighboring *Dhammasaṅgaṇī* sections—including *Lokuttarakusala* (Ds 2.1.5), *Dvādasa akusala* (Ds 2.1.6), and *Abyākatavipāka* (Ds 2.1.7)—as well as the *Vibhaṅga* (Vb 6, 12, 15) and commentaries such as the *Dhammasaṅgaṇi-aṭṭhakathā* [DharmaNexus]. In cross-language matches, DharmaNexus automatically aligns the text with Sanskrit and Tibetan scholastic works treating mental constituents and definitions, notably the *Arthaviniścayasūtra* and its commentary, Śāntideva's *Śikṣāsamuccaya*, Asaṅga's *Abhidharmasamuccaya*, and the *Śrāvakabhūmi* of the *Yogācārabhūmi* [DharmaNexus].
